front.title: Recovery Admission: Pre-Execution Authorization for Self-Healing Actions in Agentic Systems

abstract.t: This document defines Recovery Admission: the authorization control plane governing whether an automated recovery action (retry, degrade, failover, request-rewrite) may execute. Recovery Admission is distinct from gateway authorization: it applies AFTER the gateway admits the original request, in the seconds during which an agent decides how to recover from failure. Each admission decision is made on four independent dimensions (delegated identity, tool version, side-effect class, runtime state), and each executed action is bound to a tamper-evident receipt. The specification ships with a falsifiable 576-vector conformance suite whose expected verdicts are generated by a decision table and verified by an independent implementation.

section.title: Introduction
section.t: Agent systems fail and recover automatically. Retry, degradation, failover and request-rewrite decisions execute in seconds, without human gatekeeping. Existing infrastructure (service meshes, API gateways, workflow-recovery engines, SOAR runbooks) treats these moments as reliability problems. None of them answers the authorization question: is this recovery action itself authorized?

The gap is structural. A gateway decides on the original request; nobody decides on the recovery. A workflow engine retries; whether the retry may widen scope, switch subject, or rewrite a request is a policy decision nobody recorded. This document fills that gap: fail-and-recover, not fail-closed.

section.title: Terminology
section.t: Recovery Action: an automated action executed in response to a prior failure (classes: readonly, state-write, failover, irreversible).
Admission Decision: a pre-execution verdict, one of ALLOW, DOWNGRADE, FAILSOVER-REBIND, HOLD, ESCALATE, REFUSES, with a machine-checkable reason class.

Two delegation tracks are distinguished. In the chain track, the acting principal's authority derives from a delegation chain; verdicts bind the chain tail and revocation propagates down-chain. In the no-chain track, authority rests on local assertions only; verdicts bind locally and every state-mutating action fails closed (no-chain-cannot-bind-state-action).

section.title: The Four Admission Dimensions
section.t: 1. Identity. Delegated principal resolution: chain shape (valid / tail-mismatch / broken / none), tail binding, and revocation with propagation semantics — revoking an intermediate principal invalidates the whole downstream chain (identity-revoked-propagated), while a local revocation without a chain yields a distinct reason code (identity-revoked-local).

2. Tool version. A major-version drift between approved and dispatched tool refuses admission (version-major-drift). Patch versions are compatible; irreversible actions additionally require exact-version match.

3. Side effect. Four classes with decreasing permissiveness: readonly (may proceed on local assertions in the no-chain track), state-write (degrades when runtime is stale), failover (requires fresh subject-binding re-signature; refuses without: failover-without-fresh-sbsr), irreversible (human gate whenever runtime is not fresh or version is not exact: ESCALATE/human-gate-required).

4. Runtime state. Fresh, stale, or upstream-down. Upstream-down holds reversible actions with intent-hash preservation (intent-hash-preserved-no-silent-rewrite) — the system may not silently rewrite a request while the upstream is unavailable.

section.title: Decision Semantics
section.t: Evaluation order is normative: integrity first (a tampered args-digest refuses every local assertion: integrity-digest-tampered), then delegation structure (track, shape, tail, revocation), then version, then the runtime/side-effect matrix. DOWNGRADE never widens scope. FAILSOVER-REBIND requires a fresh subject-binding signature. Request-rewrites preserve the original intent hash. Learned rules enter a shadow ledger and never auto-execute.

section.title: Receipt Binding
section.t: Every decision — including refuses, holds and breaker states — emits a signed, hash-chained receipt binding the correlation id, decision, reason class, and the canonical-JSON digest of the effective arguments. Receipt continuity is the audit substrate for "who decided, on what evidence, when".

section.title: Security Considerations
section.t: The expected verdicts in the conformance suite are generated by a decision table and re-derived by an independent implementation; this catches table/checker divergence but cannot catch a shared wrong assumption. Reviewers are invited to dispute specific anchor verdicts by identifier. The digest-only verification column (verifying receipts without the four-dimension admission) is included to demonstrate concretely what a weaker pipeline would wrongly accept: in the shipped suite it accepts 288 intact-digest anchors that full admission refuses.

section.title: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document has no IANA actions.

section.title: Appendix A: 576-Vector Conformance Suite
section.t: Six orthogonal dimensions (delegation 4 x revocation 2 x version 3 x side-effect 4 x runtime 3 x integrity 2) yield 576 anchors. The public, runnable suite lives at https://github.com/DSHCorrectover/correctover-recovery-admission (Apache-2.0 code, CC0 data): two commands reproduce 576/576 agreement between the decision table and the independent verifier, plus a tamper self-test that must be caught.

Verdict distribution (measured, not tuned): ALLOW 15, HOLD 6, DOWNGRADE 2, ESCALATE 3, REFUSES 550. Reason classes are split so that structural refusal (delegation-broken-chain 72, delegation-tail-mismatch 72), propagated vs local revocation (36/36), integrity (288) and genuine policy refusals are separately machine-checkable.

Provenance binding: the vector dataset carries its own DOI (Zenodo, CC0, DOI TBD-ON-PUBLISH) so that this draft references an immutable, citable snapshot instead of a mutable repository; the record cross-references this draft via related-identifier, closing a mutual-evidence loop (draft cites DOI; DOI cites draft; GitHub mirror carries the DOI badge). Any reader can re-verify the claimed agreement with two commands from the record.

section.title: Appendix B: Related Work Position
section.t: Workflow-recovery engines, auto-remediation and SOAR runbooks recover; they do not authorize the recovery. API gateways authorize the original request; they are silent after admission. This specification occupies the intersection: pre-execution authorization FOR recovery actions, with tamper-evident post-execution binding.
